- [ ] [2.2-S] Moving-body and force-context seams landed (`MovingBodies` + `BallSolver::step_with_bodies`, `ExternalForce::force_in` with `ForceContext`, ball add/remove notifications); 2.3/2.4/2.7 build on DECISIONS "2.2-S — moving-body and force-context seams". Owners have three documented obligations: one-sided inverse mass, real (zero) velocity on an engaged end stop, and speculative stops (never predict more travel toward a stop than it allows within the tick). Fix rounds 1–3 added a robust two-body solve (observed response, impulse cap from the contact's own effect, 100 m/s speed backstop, per-ball work budget), a joint re-solve of balls sharing one body, a pinch-only early-out and an optional body-supplied restitution (`MovingBodies::restitution`). No decision needed. [2.2-S round 3 → 2.7] `spec_2_7_magnus::prop_free_flight` fails on a high-spin case under gravity (error 2.3 % vs the 1 % bound); a plain `S·ω×v` hook gives the same error, so it is the 2.2 sub-step force integration (force at `v + g·h`, not the midpoint), not 2.7 code; the failing seed is now in `spec_2_7_magnus.proptest-regressions` (added by a 2.2-S test run). (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)

No decision needed unless you want the residual only with the coil off. (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)

(b) the coil build-up time (16 ms), its collapse time (2 ms), the rubber loss speed (2 m/s) and the bat height (30 mm) are `FlipperTuning` constants, not Appendix C tunables — add them to `physics_defaults.toml` for the Gate A1 search? (c) with the default inertia (1e-4 kg·m²) and hold torque (0.15 N·m) a 3.5 m/s ball knocks a held flipper all the way down; real flippers feel stiffer — raise the hold torque / inertia defaults at Gate A1? - [ ] [2.3 Orchestrator rulings] Timing-sweep reference: the flip time is measured from contact with the held (raised) bat, which passes at 22.8 % of the held rebound but only at the −20 ms edge. Measured from contact with the resting bat, the minimum within ±20 ms is 85.6 %. Please confirm flipper feel (live catch, tap pass) in Gate A1 or acceptance. With default parameters the exit speed from 25 % of the bat is 2.74 m/s, under the 3–7 m/s window (other contact points are inside); Gate A1 tunes this. (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)
- [ ] [2.3 review → Gate A1] Flipper feel: (a) the timing-sweep dead spot is real physics. The bat's momentum cancels the ball's as the bat reaches its end stop. A rigid end stop gives a cliff on the early side: shifting arrival by 0.1 ms changes the rebound from 0.06 to 2.07 m/s. A compliant end stop would smooth it. (b) With the default inertia (1e-4 kg·m²) and hold torque (0.15 N·m), a held bat is knocked down by balls of 2 m/s and faster, so the "held rebound" is a knock-down followed by an EOS re-power kick. Retune hold torque and inertia for a solid held flipper. (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)
- [ ] [2.3 fix round 1] Rubber: `rubber_restitution` and `rubber_damping` now act as documented, `e(u) = rubber_restitution / (1 + rubber_damping · u / 4 m/s)` on the approach speed (the earlier note that `rubber_restitution` only capped a loss is obsolete). The reference speed (4 m/s) is a `FlipperTuning` constant you may want as an Appendix C tunable. (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)
- [ ] [2.3 fix round 1 → Gate A1] The live-catch dead spot is real but narrow and not robust: ≤ 25 % of the held rebound in all 14 variants for contacts at 70 % of the bat, in none of 14 at 50 % within −20…0 ms (inertia/torque ±10 %, ball 3.3–3.7 m/s; DECISIONS "2.3 — fix round 1"). Two model-level options for Gate A1: (a) a compliant end stop (the bat decelerates over a few degrees or milliseconds instead of in one tick) would remove the rigid-stop cliff and widen the catch window; (b) the default hold torque (0.15 N·m) and inertia (1e-4 kg·m²) make a held bat non-solid (a 3.5 m/s ball knocks it down and the EOS re-power kicks it back), which is what the "held rebound" reference measures today. (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)
- [ ] [Orchestrator ruling, 2.3 criterion 1] The timing-sweep criterion is gated at outer-bat contact (70 % of the bat), and mid-bat (50 %) is reported only. At 50 % the minimum is 29–80 % of the held rebound across ±10 % parameter variants; at 70 % it is 0–17 %. Several steps above 0.75 m/s between neighbouring 1 ms flips come from the rigid end stop. Please confirm, or ask Gate A1 to change the model (compliant stop, stiffer hold). (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)
- [ ] [Orchestrator ruling, supersedes the previous 2.3 criterion-1 line] Gate A1 now owns the plan's "dead-flip minimum ≤ 25 % of the held rebound". The 2.3 gate requires a dead spot of ≤ 50 % and continuity with every jump explained. With the defaults the depth is rig-dependent: 0–21 % (Implementer's rigs, 70 % contact), 26.3 % (Tester's rig, 70 %), 24–80 % at mid-bat. Gate A1 should tune inertia, torques and stop restitution (and consider a compliant stop) to reach 25 % robustly. Please confirm this move. (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)
- [ ] [2.4 fix round 1] Corrections to the 2.4 line above: spinner now has gravity and pivot friction (`[mechs.spinner] friction` = 60 rad/s²; a 1 m/s ball gives 4 pulses, 1.5 m/s 10, 3 m/s ~32; below ~0.9 m/s no pulse); kickback 3.8 m/s; sling 1.9–3.3 m/s. Integration notes for 2.5/6.0: build `MechSpec` with `MechSpec::from_def` (mm→m inside; keep it consistent with the loader's frame, `+z` = playfield normal) since `MechSi` has no parameters (or give pin_assets an additive params field); diverter, gate and newton_ball mechs are inert in `MechSet` and must be wired by 2.5 (diverter → `StaticWorld::set_enabled`, newton_ball → `NewtonChain`); a VUK stops a ball at any speed on capture, and the 60 mm eject jump will show in render interpolation; `MechSet::step` needs `events.clear()` every tick. The 2.4 spec tests of the spinner (Tester) encode the old pure-exponential model and need updating to the documented B2 model. (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)
- [ ] [2.3 review round 2 → Gate A1] Three levers and limits of the flipper model: (N1) in the tick in which the bat reaches a stop, 2.3 slows the bat's whole surface to `(stop − θ)/(dt − t)`, which is more conservative than the seam's restated obligation 3 (limit only this tick's drive increment and carry the held momentum into the stop) — a lever on the depth and continuity of the live-catch dead spot; (N3) the seam's restitution hook does not know the ball's material, so `rubber_restitution` (with `rubber_damping`) now applies to every ball profile on a flipper — ceramic and plastic balls previously got 0.78 / 0.84 from the pair table; (N4) the mid-bat gate (dead spot ≤ 50 % of the held rebound) is thin under +10 % power torque (51–58 %). (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)

- [ ] [Orchestrator, 2.7 Magnus fix] Plain `Magnus` assumes the default gravity (0, 0, −9.81), and `register_all` uses the solver's own gravity through `MagnusWithGravity`. A table that changes gravity must register Magnus with that gravity. Cleaner: add gravity to `ForceContext` the next time `ball/` is opened. (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)
- [ ] [2.7 fix-task review N7–N9 → next `ball/` change] Plain `Magnus` exceeds the 1 % bound when the solver's gravity is far from the default: 2.4 % at zero g, 1.8 % at moon gravity, 2.3 % with a 29.4 m/s² sideways gravity. `register_all` captures gravity once, so a later `BallSolver::set_gravity` reproduces that bias; nothing in src calls `set_gravity` today. In contact, the midpoint velocity carries a spurious g·h/2 normal component, worth about 2e-3 m/s² at most. Fix: add `gravity` to `ForceContext` and have Magnus read it, which retires `MagnusWithGravity`. (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)

- [ ] [issue-8] Curved Newton-chain contacts use the effective-mass impulse projected onto each ball's path tangent. World momentum along the centre line is conserved only for straight or symmetric geometry; the path takes the rest. The hairpin regression test uses arms 1.2R–1.8R apart, not "2R to 3R" as briefed, because balls on arms 2R or more apart cannot touch. `closest_point` queries near a centre of curvature now cost 1.3–2.7× (still under 1 µs). See DECISIONS.md "issue-8 — …". (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)

See DECISIONS.md "issue-8 — separate() positional correction on curved paths (CodeRabbit E)". (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)
- [ ] [issue-8] CodeRabbit F/G: `separate` now moves a ball that would reach or pass its other neighbour only halfway to it (keeps the chain strictly ordered; 8 balls packed at one stop take ~90 steps to spread out). `advance` caps zero-time stop events at 2n per step and drifts any unspent step time. Both are judgement calls. See DECISIONS.md "issue-8 — separate() order handling when spill inverts a pair (CodeRabbit F)" and "issue-8 — advance() zero-time stop/contact cycles (CodeRabbit G)". (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)

- [ ] [pin_script-callback-cost] Approve a pin_script follow-up (pre-existing since PR #3, not Wave 6): `Bridge::releases_pending()` scans 1024 words on every Lua callback and `Vm::reset_budget` calls `set_hook_count` through mlua exec_raw on every callback, together about 10 % of tick cost on the replay fixture. Fix plan: an O(1) pending-release count in crates/pin_script/src/lua/bridge.rs, and restore the hook count only when it was lowered (crates/pin_script/src/lua/sandbox.rs); no simulation output change expected. See DECISIONS wave6-gate-benchmark. (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)
- [ ] [w7pre-backbox-colliders] Confirm: with a `backbox_colliders.glb`, the backbox geometry and the flippers on its layers grow the escape box instead of the playfield bounds (the playfield glass keeps its height) and the playfield glass leaves the backbox layers out; tables without the file are unchanged. A backbox layer shared with a playfield collider, spline, or a flipper whose base is outside the backbox geometry is a load error (CodeRabbit r4606779403). See DECISIONS.md "w7pre-backbox-colliders — backbox colliders in the runtime world". (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)

Open: the warning runs in the generator (`pin_tablegen <layout>`) only; also running it from `pin_tablegen validate` (`src/clearance/checks.rs` `transitions`, which needs the collider triangles it already has) was outside this item's owned paths. The grey-box's `ramp_catch_below` was split around the new zone. (docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md)

The layer-2 deck (z 0.1, y 560..692.5) covers them in plan; a ball below the deck there has no catch. Combined Gate A1 (3000 balls) shows no effect (0 stuck, endless or escaped). ## 4. D33 flags

- Ray-query reflections ship off by default unless validated by a ray-tracing runner.
- The DOF bridge (Windows package only) ships marked "unverified on hardware" (`dof_bridge/UNVERIFIED.txt`).
- Release artifacts are unsigned (no Authenticode, no macOS Developer ID or notarization; macOS gets an ad-hoc signature only).

Mentions of D33 in the run log, queue and decisions:

- docs/DECISIONS.md: **Fallback (adapters without the bit, e.g. GL here):** the D18/§6 baseline — octahedral reflection probes — selected at runtime from the adapter's feature set; ray-query reflections stay off by default (D33). Lavapipe reporting the bit may let Subphase 5.4 validate the ray-query path on the Linux CI runner (functional, not performance).
- docs/DECISIONS.md: **Consequences.** Only Linux lavapipe can exercise the ray-query path in hosted CI; Windows and macOS validate the probe fallback (D18, D33). macOS reports no `Mailbox`, so secondary surfaces there use `Immediate` or a presenter thread (D19). The local Mesa in Q3 above (25.2.8) differs from CI (26.0.8); answers agree.
- docs/DECISIONS.md: - **3.5 ownership.** `tools/dof_bridge/` (.NET 8), a new `pin_app::dof` launcher module (one `mod` line in `pin_app/src/lib.rs`), a `[dof]` cross-reference check in `pin_assets` validation, and a new Windows-only `dof-bridge` CI job. The `[dof]` schema already exists in `pin_core` (1.1). Calling the launcher on table load is 6.0's. Real DOF is loaded by reflection behind an `IDofSink`, so CI uses a mock sink (D33: "unverified on hardware").
- docs/DECISIONS.md: Status: **contract for the 3.5 Tester** (kept current by the Implementer). Real DOF hosting is "unverified on hardware" (D33).
- docs/DECISIONS.md: - **Decision (real DOF path).** `ReflectionDofSink` loads `DirectOutput.Pinball` by reflection and calls `Setup(globalConfig, tableName, romName)`, `Init()`, `ReceiveData(char,int,int)`, `Finish()`; tested only against a fake `DirectOutput.dll` (`tests/support/FakeDirectOutput`). **Unverified on hardware (D33).**
- docs/DECISIONS.md: - **Decision (skip policy).** Ray-mode tests skip with a note when the adapter lacks the feature. Under `PIN_REQUIRE_GPU=1` they fail when the adapter is lavapipe (known to report the bit) or when the adapter reports the bit but `GpuContext::new_headless` created the device without it. They do not fail on WARP or Metal adapters that lack it, because CI sets `PIN_REQUIRE_GPU=1` on every OS and D33 makes ray queries optional. `PIN_REQUIRE_RAY_QUERY=1` turns any skip into a failure.
- docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md: - [3.5] DOF bridge choices to confirm (DECISIONS "3.5 — DOF bridge design choices"): resolved map passed as a temp JSON file, stop = stdin EOF + 1.5 s grace then kill, GI driven via `lamp =` mappings to `kind = "gi"` lamps (no `gi =` key in `[dof]`), lamp value round(v·255). Real DOF hosting (reflection on `DirectOutput.Pinball`) is unverified on hardware (D33) — please try it on a cabinet.
- docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md: - [3.5 review round 1, non-blocking] (N2) A late datagram of an OLDER full state arriving after a newer one is taken as a new session (protocol §6 mandates it) and regresses elements until the next full state; needs ~1 s of reordering — known limitation. (N3) After a restart, map entries carried by a lost full-state datagram are forwarded later only if their value differs (DOF state stays consistent; deviation from "sends everything"). (N10) The real Windows spawn path (CREATE_NO_WINDOW, stdin-EOF stop, kill after grace, .exe quoting) is not run by any CI job — unverified, like real DOF (D33). (N12) --parent-pid is open to pid reuse and treats access-denied as dead; stdin EOF covers the normal case.
- docs/HUMAN_QUEUE.md: - [5.4 CR round 1] DX12 / Metal ray-query hardware survey still open (PLAN risk row 5): only Vulkan (lavapipe) was observed to report EXPERIMENTAL_RAY_QUERY on wgpu 30.0.1; a run on real DX12 and Metal hardware would confirm or change the "ray path only when the device reports the feature" selection. Ray queries stay OFF by default (D33).
- docs/decisions/2026-11-20-7.2.md: "blocked" (case-insensitive). Gate lines match `[Gg]ate A<n>` or `[Ww]ave <n> gate`. D33
- docs/decisions/2026-11-20-7.2.md: mentions match `D33` not preceded by a letter or digit and not followed by a digit. All inputs

## 6. Phase 8 checklist

- [ ] **1. Review the run.** Read sections 1 to 5, every open line in `docs/queue/` and the decisions in `docs/decisions/`; rule on each open item.
- [ ] **2. Play each table.** Check flipper feel, ball speed, catches and nudge. Tune only data (`physics_defaults.toml` or the table TOML), rerun CI, and confirm Gates A1 and A2 revalidate.
  - [ ] greybox: flipper feel, ball speed, catches, nudge
  - [ ] apex_circuit: flipper feel, ball speed, catches, nudge
  - [ ] sky_deck: flipper feel, ball speed, catches, nudge
  - [ ] feature_lab: flipper feel, ball speed, catches, nudge
  - [ ] Any tuning is data-only (`physics_defaults.toml` / table TOML); CI rerun; Gates A1 and A2 revalidate
- [ ] **3. Check hardware.**
  - [ ] X-Arcade in each mode
  - [ ] Analog plunger
  - [ ] Accelerometer nudge
  - [ ] Rumble
  - [ ] SSF channels
  - [ ] Multi-monitor layout
  - [ ] DOF devices (the bridge ships unverified on hardware, D33)
- [ ] **4. Check visuals.**
  - [ ] Reflections, bloom, DMD and backglass on a real display
  - [ ] Ray-query reflections on a capable GPU, then decide whether to enable them by default (D33)
- [ ] **5. Replace placeholders.** Swap in real sounds, music, callouts and art by asset ID.
